NG.title: Nnamdi Azikiwe
NG.note: Known as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism', Nnamdi Azikiwe was Nigeria's first President (1963–1966) and a key figure in the country's independence movement.

NG.title: Obafemi Awolowo
NG.note: A nationalist and statesman, Obafemi Awolowo was the first Premier of the Western Region and a key advocate for free education and healthcare in Nigeria.

NG.title: Ahmadu Bello
NG.note: The Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of the Northern Region, Ahmadu Bello was a prominent leader who worked to modernize the north and promote unity in Nigeria.

NG.title: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti
NG.note: A pioneering feminist and activist, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti fought for women's rights and was the first woman in Nigeria to drive a car.

NG.title: Herbert Macaulay
NG.note: Regarded as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism', Herbert Macaulay was a key figure in the fight for independence and the founder of Nigeria's first political party.

NG.title: Chinua Achebe
NG.note: One of Africa's greatest novelists, Chinua Achebe's 'Things Fall Apart' is a classic of modern African literature, exploring themes of colonialism and tradition.

NG.title: Wole Soyinka
NG.note: The first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1986), Wole Soyinka is a playwright, poet, and activist known for his works on justice and human rights.

NG.title: Fela Kuti
NG.note: The pioneer of Afrobeat music, Fela Kuti used his music to criticize corruption and military rule in Nigeria, becoming a symbol of resistance.

NG.title: Mary Slessor
NG.note: A Scottish missionary who lived in Calabar, Mary Slessor is remembered for her efforts to end the killing of twins and promote education in Nigeria.

NG.title: Usman dan Fodio
NG.note: A religious scholar and reformer, Usman dan Fodio led the Fulani Jihad of 1804, founding the Sokoto Caliphate, one of the largest empires in 19th-century Africa.

NG.title: Alvan Ikoku
NG.note: An educationist and nationalist, Alvan Ikoku was a key advocate for free and universal primary education in Nigeria.

NG.title: Margaret Ekpo
NG.note: A women's rights activist and politician, Margaret Ekpo was one of Nigeria's first female political leaders and a strong advocate for women's participation in politics.

NG.title: Tafawa Balewa
NG.note: Nigeria's first Prime Minister (1960–1966), Tafawa Balewa was a key figure in the country's transition to independence.

NG.title: Ken Saro-Wiwa
NG.note: An environmental activist and writer, Ken Saro-Wiwa led the Ogoni struggle against environmental degradation caused by oil exploration in the Niger Delta.

NG.title: Queen Amina of Zazzau
NG.note: A legendary warrior queen of Zazzau (Zaria), Queen Amina expanded her kingdom and is remembered as a symbol of strength and leadership.

NG.title: Blessing Okagbare
NG.note: An Olympic medalist and world champion sprinter and long jumper, Blessing Okagbare is one of Nigeria's most celebrated athletes.

NG.title: Hajiya Gambo Sawaba
NG.note: A women's rights activist and politician, Hajiya Gambo Sawaba fought for the rights of women and the underprivileged in northern Nigeria.

NG.title: Anthony Enahoro
NG.note: A nationalist and politician, Anthony Enahoro moved the first motion for Nigeria's independence in 1953.

NG.title: Florence Nwanzuruahu Nkiru Nwapa
NG.note: Known as the 'Mother of African Literature', Flora Nwapa was the first African woman to publish a novel in English.

NG.title: Yakubu Gowon
NG.note: Nigeria's youngest Head of State, Yakubu Gowon led the country during the Civil War (1967–1970) and initiated the 'no victor, no vanquished' policy.

NG.title: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
NG.note: The first woman and first African to serve as the Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO), Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is a globally recognized economist and former Nigerian Finance Minister.

NG.title: Akinwumi Adesina
NG.note: The President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Akinwumi Adesina is a renowned economist and former Nigerian Minister of Agriculture, known for his agricultural reforms.

NG.title: Burna Boy
NG.note: A Grammy-winning artist, Burna Boy is one of Nigeria's most prominent musicians, using his Afrobeat music to address social and political issues.

NG.title: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
NG.note: An award-winning author and feminist, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is known for her novels and essays that explore themes of identity, feminism, and post-colonialism.

NG.title: Tony Elumelu
NG.note: A billionaire entrepreneur and philanthropist, Tony Elumelu is the founder of the Tony Elumelu Foundation, which empowers African entrepreneurs.

NG.title: Tems
NG.note: A globally recognized singer and songwriter, Tems has gained international acclaim for her contributions to Afrobeat and collaborations with global artists.

NG.title: Olusegun Obasanjo
NG.note: A former Nigerian President and influential statesman, Olusegun Obasanjo remains active in African diplomacy and governance.

NG.title: Aliko Dangote
NG.note: The richest man in Africa, Aliko Dangote is a business magnate and philanthropist, known for his contributions to Nigeria's industrial development.

NG.title: Tobi Amusan
NG.note: A world champion hurdler, Tobi Amusan is a record-breaking athlete who has brought global recognition to Nigerian sports.

NG.title: Aisha Yesufu
NG.note: A prominent activist and co-founder of the #BringBackOurGirls movement, Aisha Yesufu is known for her advocacy for human rights and good governance.

NG.title: Davido
NG.note: One of Nigeria's most popular musicians, Davido has gained international fame for his Afrobeat music and philanthropic efforts.

NG.title: Peter Obi
NG.note: A former Governor of Anambra State and a prominent political figure, Peter Obi is known for his focus on governance, transparency, and economic reforms.

NG.title: Rabiu Kwankwaso
NG.note: A former Governor of Kano State and influential political leader, Rabiu Kwankwaso is known for his educational reforms and grassroots mobilization.

NG.title: Blessing Abeng
NG.note: A branding and communications expert, Blessing Abeng is the co-founder of Ingressive for Good, an organization focused on empowering African youth with tech skills.
